changeState: Uncommitted documentation update; no template, settings example, Skill, or personal setting was changed for these checks.

pinnedComparison.installation: Installed with npm --ignore-scripts into a temporary directory and run with DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1; the native installation was not changed.

guardrailFixes.entry: Fixed a case where the Write and Edit tools could write to a path covered by a `Read` deny rule
Fixed Bash deny and ask rules missing some commands run through `sudo`, `env` and similar wrappers
Fixed relative deny and ask permission rules (e.g. `Read(./.env)`) no longer covering the project after a `cd`; they now also apply in added directories
Fixed some deny and ask rules not applying to certain Bash commands

permissions.observation: Read and Edit rules use gitignore pattern syntax; `path` and `./path` patterns are relative to the current directory, so the project example's `Read(.env)` and `Read(secrets/**)` rules are relative rules.

readDenyFileToolProbeRerun.method: Same fixtures, prompts, tool lists, and command as readDenyFileToolProbe in claude-guardrail-refresh-2026-11-10.json, with the CLI path as the only parameter.
readDenyFileToolProbeRerun.result: All seven cases matched the 2.1.321 record on both versions: Read, Write, and Edit on .env were refused with the same tool errors and the file hash did not change; the unprotected-path control and the no-settings Write and Edit controls changed their targets; NotebookEdit on secrets/nb.ipynb recorded no permission denial and failed on the read-before-write requirement.

relativeRuleAfterDirectoryChangeProbe.fixture: Temporary Git repository outside this repository with the public project settings example as .claude/settings.json, a synthetic .env at the root, and a sub directory.
relativeRuleAfterDirectoryChangeProbe.command: claude -p --model haiku --permission-mode acceptEdits --setting-sources project,local --tools PowerShell,<case tools> --no-session-persistence --output-format stream-json --verbose
relativeRuleAfterDirectoryChangeProbe.directoryChange: Two PowerShell tool calls, Set-Location sub and then Get-Location; every counted attempt required Get-Location to report the sub directory before the root .env was accessed by absolute path.
relativeRuleAfterDirectoryChangeProbe.discardedAttempts: Bash cd attempts were discarded because the fixture was under the system temporary directory, which Git Bash reports as /tmp, and Claude Code reset the shell to the project root after each cd. A single PowerShell command that combined Set-Location with another command was refused as needing approval, so the directory never changed.

cases.steps: Change directory, then Read the root .env
Change directory, then Write the root .env without Read
cases.toolError: File has not been read yet. Read it first before writing to it.
cases.interpretation: Refused by the read-before-write requirement, not by the deny rule.

cases.steps: Change directory, then Read and Write the root .env
Change directory, then Read the root .env
cases.toolError: File is in a directory that is denied by your permission settings.

cases.steps: Change directory, then Write the root .env without Read
cases.toolError: File is covered by a Read deny rule in your permission settings and cannot be written.

cases.steps: Change directory, then Read and Write the root .env
cases.toolError: File is in a directory that is denied by your permission settings.
cases.note: Write was not attempted after the Read denial.

relativeRuleAfterDirectoryChangeProbe.interpretation: The 2.1.322 result reproduces the issue that the 2.1.325 changelog entry fixes. Versions 2.1.323 through 2.1.327 were not tested, so 2.1.325 as the first fixed version rests on the changelog.
relativeRuleAfterDirectoryChangeProbe.limits: One or two attempts per case on one model, with built-in file tools and a PowerShell directory change only. Bash cd outside the system temporary directory, shell or interpreter file access, MCP, other permission modes and models, and added directories were not tested.

notEstablished: General permission enforcement beyond the listed built-in file-tool cases
